assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1 to long-acting agonists, produced one of the largest therapeutic shifts in metabolic medicine, with effects on diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular outcomes. The conceptual chain from gut hormone biology to drugs is clear and has had lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established GLP-1 biology and its physiological and therapeutic roles; Mojsov's work on the active peptide form is a distinct, contested-in-public contribution. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen is credited for the drug-development side, which is industrial and could instead be left to other recognition. Whether three is the fairest configuration is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, large randomized outcome trials and widespread clinical use. Recognition is timely and the field is highly visible.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and early therapeutic proof of concept is disputed in the literature, and I have not verified details independently.
Drug-development contributions (e.g. liraglutide, semaglutide) may sit awkwardly with a discovery-based prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with millisecond precision. The discovery of channelrhodopsins as light-gated channels, followed by their use in neurons, transformed experimental biology well beyond neuroscience.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterized channelrhodopsin as a light-gated cation channel. Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated neuronal control; Miesenboeck contributed an earlier genetically targeted photoactivation concept. Six credited names exceed the three-person limit, so the configuration is hard and contested. I propose the channel discovery plus the main neuronal-application leader.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed, with massive independent use over roughly two decades. Timely or arguably overdue given the field's maturity; clinical use (retinal optogenetic vision restoration) is early.
uncertainties: Priority among Boyden, Deisseroth, Miesenboeck and Bamberg is unresolved and would likely exclude people with strong claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed against tumour antigens produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and established a new class of living drugs. The impact on oncology and immunology is large and clear.
assessment.attribution: June (CD19 CAR-T clinical translation with 4-1BB), Sadelain (CD28-costimulated CARs and preclinical foundations) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T cells) are central. Eshhar's early chimeric receptor work and others are not on the supplied list, so the credit picture is incomplete here.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and several years of follow-up show durable responses in blood cancers. Limits remain in solid tumours and toxicity management, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Early chimeric-receptor priority is not represented in the credited names.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, is still being assessed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR as the target of rapamycin and of mTOR as the central nutrient and growth sensor reshaped cell growth, metabolism, ageing and cancer biology. The conceptual clarity and breadth of the mechanism are excellent.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically in yeast and is the pivotal contributor. Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin and Sabatini's mTOR identification and nutrient-sensing pathway work are major mammalian extensions; others (Heitman, Movva and colleagues, Brown, Sabatini's lab members) also contributed to the chemistry and target identification. The allocation is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed across species and in many labs. Clinical use of rapalogs in transplantation and oncology is established, and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Credit for the mammalian target identification was shared among several groups and I am uncertain of the precise priority chronology.
Therapeutic utility in ageing is not yet proven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined an intracellular signalling pathway from the ER lumen to the nucleus, with relevance to secretory physiology, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. It is a clean and original mechanistic discovery.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the central figures: Mori for the identification of the UPR transcriptional response and Ire1/Hac1 pathways, Walter for Ire1 mechanism and unconventional splicing. The two-person configuration is coherent, with Ron/Harding on PERK a possible additional claim outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism is well confirmed across organisms for many years. Clinical translation is still in development, but the basic discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Contributions of PERK/ATF6 branches may require wider recognition than the supplied names allow.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL kinase inhibition with imatinib converted chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal to a manageable disease and validated molecularly targeted therapy. Its conceptual influence on cancer drug development is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Druker led clinical translation, Lydon the compound programme, and Sawyers the resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors. The three names map onto distinct decisive steps, though the underlying oncogene discovery (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore) is not on the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with long-term survival data and decades of independent confirmation. Recognition is somewhat late, and prior Lasker awards exist.
uncertainties: Whether a prize centred on drug development is favoured over discovery science is unclear.
Earlier BCR-ABL genetics credit is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explained how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immune and interferon responses, with implications for infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and ageing. The mechanistic discovery of cGAMP as a second messenger is original and conceptually clean.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP, the decisive step. Barber identified STING; Ishikawa is credited for STING work as well, and Sun and Wu were Chen's lab members. A two-person configuration seems most defensible but is open to dispute over STING priority.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in structural and genetic studies, but therapeutic translation is still in early clinical stages, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: STING priority between Barber and Ishikawa and Ishii-Akira is not fully resolved in my knowledge.
Clinical benefit is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identifying BCL11A as the repressor of fetal haemoglobin explained the haemoglobin switch and led to an approved gene-editing therapy for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassaemia. It links human genetics, regulatory biology and therapy elegantly.
assessment.attribution: Orkin and Sankaran defined BCL11A's role in globin switching, and Bauer contributed enhancer-targeting strategies underlying the therapy. Swee Lay Thein's GWAS-related contribution is also credited and could support an alternative configuration. The decisive allocation between genetics, mechanism and editing is not settled.
assessment.maturity: Approval and early patient data are compelling, but follow-up is short. Recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Long-term durability and safety of edited cells are still emerging.
Contribution of GWAS-based discovery versus mechanism work is difficult to apportion.
